caption_recommended:
I thought love would remember the versions of me that worked.

Turns out, it also remembers the crossed-out plans, the first drafts, and the selves I was ready to call a waste.

Maybe being known is having someone see a life where you only saw almosts.
caption_alt: For the person who saw a story in the versions of you that you almost threw away.

A worn unlabelled folder has just landed in the carton. Aachu's right hand has released it while Zuv bends and retrieves its edge with a fully traceable right arm. Aachu faces the drawer and is already moving to the next item; Zuv's gaze and torso point only toward the folder. Illustrated carousel slide 2: Tactile close insert at floor level. The rescued folder lies open between them. Several dog-eared unfinished paper forms fan out: erased pencil marks, blank-line layouts, rough boxes and folded sheets, but no readable words, names, dates, applications, courses, employers, titles, grades or signatures. Aachu begins to draw the cover shut while Zuv leaves space and does not tug against her. Only lower torsos, connected forearms and knees enter frame. Exactly two people and no other figures or reflections.

Illustrated carousel slide 3: True overhead chronology view on the floor or low table. Zuv lays four or five visually distinct, non-readable sheets into a clean left-to-right progression. Paper wear and construction style shift subtly from older to fresher. Aachu sits opposite, watching with one hand held close to her knee. The chronology itself becomes the bridge between them. Exactly two people, no reflected or background figures, and no readable secondary text.

Illustrated carousel slide 4: Over-Zuv-shoulder medium reaction view. Aachu is in sharp focus beyond the ordered papers. Her hand has released the folder cover and opened it flat beside the chronology. Her guarded posture softens into a quiet, startled half-smile. Zuv remains only a grounded shoulder and partial profile in the foreground. The paper line leads the eye from him to her face. No embrace, praise or explanatory gesture; the silence is the event. Exactly two people, no reflections or extra figures, no readable paper text.

Illustrated carousel slide 5: Low table-level close two-shot with the hand action in the foreground. Aachu slides a fresh, visibly unfinished but wordless page into the open final gap of the ordered row. Zuv has withdrawn his hands and watches from beside her. The rescued folder remains open behind the chronology. Aachu leans forward and owns the action; Zuv is close but not directing it, and both gazes converge on the new page. Exactly two people, no background figures, mirrors, portraits, silhouettes, labels, dates or readable secondary text.
